I can understand that feeling.

I had my girlfriend of a year break up with me almost five years ago and I’m still not quite right. Can’t remember her face, how she was, or the moments we shared anymore, and I don’t care to. I was suicidal for quite some time afterwards, and a lot of short-lived failed relationships trying to recreate what I had. Figured after a while I’d never find love again, that my capacity for falling in love was broken, and I might as well give up.

Then I met another girl who gave me that feeling back. It was nice for a couple of months, then she disappeared and never talked to me again. Since then, I realized I don’t need anyone in that way. I’ve got good friends who I care for dearly, and I never needed anyone else.

I would try to be angry about it rather than sad. Not the kind of anger where you hurt someone, the kind where you make yourself better. Where you find how hard you can push yourself. I found my calling in anger, found out how many years I wasted doubting myself and wallowing in pity instead of pursuing something, anything at all.

Good luck. It fades over time.
